questions.knowledge_point: Integrating Using the Squared Cosine Variant of the Cosine Double-Angle Formula
questions.worked_solution:
Here, we use the double-angle formula for cosine that involves the ${cos}^{2}⁡\theta $ term, given by

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta =2{cos}^{2}⁡\theta -1.
$$

 

Rearranging, we have

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta +1).
$$

Letting $\theta =2x$, we have

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡2x=\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡4x+1).
$$

Substituting this into our integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (5{cos}^{2}⁡2x-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})\text{d}x & =\int [5\cdot \frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡4x+1)-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]\text{d}x \\  & =\int (\frac{5}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡4x+\frac{5}{2}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{5}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡4x+\frac{5}{2}x-\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}+C \\  & =\frac{5}{8}\operatorname{sin}⁡4x+\frac{5x}{2}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{6}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Integrating Using the Squared Sine Variant of the Cosine Double-Angle Formula
questions.worked_solution:
Let's recall the double-angle formula for cosine that involves the ${sin}^{2}$ term: 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta =1-2{sin}^{2}⁡\theta .
$$

We can rearrange the above formula as

$$
1-\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta =2{sin}^{2}⁡\theta .
$$

Letting $\theta =\frac{x}{4},$ we have

$$
1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{x}{2})=2{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{x}{4}).
$$

We can now integrate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 2{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{x}{4})\,\text{d}x & =\int [1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{x}{2})]\text{d}x \\  & =x-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{x}{2})+C\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14044295/assets/86e34aa6aff8f62f1913d2f432f1236d651d3813647e512d398b51c7b7ce48f7.png)

Find the area $A$ of the region in the $xy$-plane that is bounded by the curve $y=2{cos}^{2}⁡(3x)-2{sin}^{2}⁡(3x)+{x}^{2}+4,$ the $x$-axis and the lines $x=0$ and $x=\frac{\pi }{2},$ as shown above. Do not round the answer.

$A=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
The area of the region is given by

$$
A={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(2{cos}^{2}⁡(3x)-2{sin}^{2}⁡(3x)+{x}^{2}+4)\,\text{d}x.
$$

To calculate this integral, we use the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2x={cos}^{2}⁡x-{sin}^{2}⁡x
$$

We can rewrite the above formula as

$$
2\operatorname{cos}⁡6x=2{cos}^{2}⁡(3x)-2{sin}^{2}⁡(3x).
$$

Hence, the area of the region is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(2{cos}^{2}⁡(3x)-2{sin}^{2}⁡(3x)+{x}^{2}+4)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡6x+{x}^{2}+4)\,\text{d}x \\  & =(\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡6x+\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}+4x)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =[\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\pi )+\frac{(\pi /2)^{3}}{3}+4\cdot \frac{\pi }{2}]-[\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)+\frac{{0}^{3}}{3}+4\cdot 0] \\  & =[0+\frac{{\pi }^{3}}{24}+2\pi ]-0 \\  & =\frac{{\pi }^{3}}{24}+2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Integrating Using the Squared Cosine Variant of the Cosine Double-Angle Formula
questions.worked_solution:
Here, we use the double-angle formula for cosine that involves the ${cos}^{2}⁡x$ term, given by

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2x=2{cos}^{2}⁡x-1.
$$

 

Rearranging, we have

$$
2{cos}^{2}⁡x=\operatorname{cos}⁡2x+1.
$$

Multiplying both sides by $3,$ we obtain

$$
6{cos}^{2}⁡x=3(\operatorname{cos}⁡2x+1).
$$

Substituting this into our integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }6{cos}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }3(\operatorname{cos}⁡2x+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2x+3x)|}_{\pi /2}^{\pi } \\  & =[\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi )+3\pi ]-[\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )+3\cdot \frac{\pi }{2}] \\  & =3\pi -\frac{3\pi }{2} \\  & =\frac{3\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14044295/assets/d1d49c23cebfe2979c8bff7b7f19d5435807a8d1aec348070aadfab1e9d2ca19.png)

Find the area $A$ of the region in the $xy$-plane that is bounded by the curve $y={x}^{2}-{sin}^{2}⁡(x),$ the $x$-axis, and the lines $x=\frac{\pi }{2}$ and $x=\pi ,$ as shown above. Do not round the answer.

$A=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
The area of the region bounded by the curve $y={x}^{2}-{sin}^{2}⁡x,$ the $x$-axis and the lines $x=\frac{\pi }{2}$ and $x=\pi $ is

$$
A={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }({x}^{2}-{sin}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Let's recall the double-angle formula for cosine that involves the ${sin}^{2}$ term: 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2x=1-2{sin}^{2}⁡x
$$

We can rearrange the above formula as

$$
\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2x-1)=-{sin}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Hence, the area of the region is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }({x}^{2}-{sin}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }({x}^{2}+\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2x-1))\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }({x}^{2}+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡2x-\frac{1}{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}+\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡2x-\frac{1}{2}x)|}_{\pi /2}^{\pi } \\  & =(\frac{{\pi }^{3}}{3}+\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi )-\frac{\pi }{2})-(\frac{(\pi /2)^{3}}{3}+\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )-\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =(\frac{{\pi }^{3}}{3}-\frac{\pi }{2})-(\frac{{\pi }^{3}}{24}-\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\frac{7{\pi }^{3}}{24}-\frac{\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
